Computer Science and Business Administration (BS)

Viterbi School of Engineering and the Marshall School of Business

Overview

This interdisciplinary Bachelor of Science combines the computer science core with the business administration core, preparing students to lead at the intersection of software and management. The program awards a single undergraduate degree administered jointly by the two schools; it is not a dual-degree arrangement.

Degree Requirements

A minimum of 132 units is required. All majors complete the common core and one concentration below. A grade of C or better is required in each core course.

Common Core

  1. CSCI 103 Introduction to Programming (4 units)
  2. CSCI 104 Data Structures and Object Oriented Design (4 units)
  3. BUAD 304 Organizational Behavior and Leadership (4 units)

Concentrations

Choose one concentration (three courses, 12 units):

Technology Management Concentration

  • BUAD 425 Data Analysis for Decision Making (4 units)
  • CSCI 310 Software Engineering (4 units)
  • CSCI 401 Capstone: Design and Construction of Large Software Systems (4 units)

Entrepreneurship Concentration

  • BAEP 451 The Management of New Enterprises (4 units)
  • BAEP 452 Feasibility Analysis (4 units)
  • CSCI 401 Capstone: Design and Construction of Large Software Systems (4 units)

Note: Students may petition to double-count at most one concentration course toward a minor, subject to advisor approval and school policy.
